Then I'd take item B, which fits perfectly, and finally I wouldn't take item C because it exceeds the remaining capacity. So, I'd select items A and B for the optimal solution.

If I took D based on the ratio, I would miss out on the opportunity to take E and another item that could fit within the remaining capacity. In this case, taking E could lead to a higher total value even though it has a lower ratio than D. So, I need to consider combinations of items, not just their individual ratios.

For each item, I have two choices: include it in the knapsack (if the current weight w is greater than or equal to the item's weight) or skip it. If I include the item, I add its value to the optimal solution of the remaining capacity (dp[i-1][w-weight of item]), and if I skip it, I just carry forward the optimal value without the item (dp[i-1][w]).
